To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Ki-67 proliferation is a good marker of aggressiveness in neuroendocrine neoplasm patients, that Ki-67 levels are heterogeneous among different sites of the same patient, and that the primary tumor site is a major prognostic factor.

patients with neuroendocrine neoplasm exhibiting a high Ki67 proliferation index present metastatic disease in a vast majority of cases, and depending on the primary tumor site metastases are to expected also in tumors that have low Ki67%, although they are less aggressive.

patients with GEP neuroendocrine neoplasm exhibiting a high Ki67 proliferation index present metastatic disease in a vast majority of cases, although Ki67 is a marker used to assess the aggressiveness of neuroendocrine tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the clinical relevance of Ki-67 in the assessment of GEP NEN.
the role of the proliferation marker Ki- 67 in the assessment of patients with GEP-NEN regarding the stage of disease.
the assessment of Ki-67 proliferation rate in GEP NEN and the role it plays in the evaluation of disease progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a high Ki-7 proliferation index is associated with a higher risk of metastatic disease in NEN.
the proliferation marker Ki- 67 is not useful in the assessment of the disease stage in NEN patients.
Ki-67 proliferation is not an independent prognostic factor in NEN patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ki-67 index is an important factor for assessing the stage of disease and prognosis of patients with GEP-NEN.
Ki-67 proliferation index is useful for the assessment of the stage of disease, but not for its prognosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ki-67 proportion in GEP NEN is a useful prognostic factor and should be used in the management of these patients in clinical practice.
Ki-67 proliferation rate should not be used to predict the stage of the disease.
a Ki-67 proliferation rate of less than 20 % should not be considered a reliable prognostic marker for patients with GEP-NEN.
